essentials.title: Keep to the summary in your principal's appraisal
essentials.description: From the principal's appraisal you receive only the summary result and the agreed next-year goals. You have no access to coaching records and never ask for journal content — this keeps coaching safe and the appraisal fair.

source.quote: sees only the summary triplet (score + band + recommendation) plus agreed goals for governance purposes; has no access to coaching data

essentials.title: Take up induction concerns that involve the school leader
essentials.description: When a new teacher's induction concern involves the school leader, it comes to you. Raising a concern must never disadvantage the person who raises it.

source.quote: If the concern involves the school leader, escalate to the school's Foundation Representative.

essentials.title: Keep Guidance reporting to you, separate from the principal
essentials.description: The Guidance Coordinator reports to you and works closely with the principal, but is not managed or evaluated by the principal. Keep the reporting line and the coordination line visibly different.

source.quote: Guidance reports structurally to the FR/GM and coordinates closely with Principals; Guidance is not under the Principal's managerial supervision or evaluation.

tasks.title: Confirm Academic Coordinator or Vice Principal appointments
tasks.description: The principal recommends; after governance review, you (or the authorised Foundation authority) formally confirm the appointment, and it is recorded. No one can self-activate a role, allowance or reporting authority.
tasks.timing_text: Start of the year, and whenever an appointment is recommended

source.quote: formal appointment confirmed by the FR/GM or authorized Foundation authority.

tasks.title: Join the meetings at your school's Phase 1 visit
tasks.description: On the visit day you join the principal for the presentation of school programmes, the domain meetings, the post-appraisal management meeting and the Oral Exit Report (about 15.00). There is no written report after Phase 1 — the findings are given in person.
tasks.timing_text: Your school's Phase 1 Teaching Quality Visit falls between 5 August and 18 September 2026 — check your school's own schedule

source.quote: Attendees: School principal, foundation representative, and other key program leaders if required.

tasks.title: Join the meetings at your school's Phase 3 visit
tasks.description: The Validation Visit checks the school's self-evaluation across the five domains. You join the domain meetings, the post-appraisal management meeting and the Oral Exit Report.
tasks.timing_text: Your school's Phase 3 Validation Visit falls between 7 October and 20 November 2026 — check your school's own schedule

source.quote: Attendees: School principal, foundation representative, and other key leaders (where possible).

tasks.title: Read the Annual School Quality Report domain by domain
tasks.description: Each of the five domains has its own Development Rating — there is no single school score. If school leadership disagrees with a rating, a written appeal goes to the Eduversal CAO within 10 working days of receiving the report; the two agreed priorities move into the School Development Plan within two weeks.
tasks.timing_text: Within three weeks of your Phase 3 visit — by mid-December 2026 at the latest

source.quote: The Validation Visit produces the school's Annual School Quality Report, which is shared with school leadership and the Eduversal central team.

tasks.title: Co-review and co-sign your principal's appraisal summary
tasks.description: After the Chief Academic Officer finalises the record, check that the process was fair and evidence-based, then co-sign the summary and next-year goals. You do not write the record or re-score any evidence.
tasks.applies_when: Your principal is in Year 2 or later (Year-1 principals are not formally appraised)
tasks.timing_text: Year end, after the primary appraiser signs off

source.quote: Checks procedural fairness at governance level and co-signs the summary.

tasks.title: Welcome your new principal and sign off the start of induction
tasks.description: Greet the principal personally on Day 1 and sign off the start of the induction year. Like the principal and the mentor, commit in writing to your part of the induction.

source.quote: Day 1 arrival. Your Foundation Representative personally welcomes you and signs off the start of your induction.

tasks.title: Give the new principal a joint handover briefing
tasks.description: Together with the Academic Coordinator and the DSL, brief the new principal on open safeguarding cases, staff matters, Cambridge centre obligations and the next entry deadline, commitments made to you, and key parent relationships.
tasks.applies_when: Your principal is in Year 1 and the previous principal left suddenly
tasks.timing_text: Before or at the new principal's arrival

source.quote: If a predecessor exists but left suddenly, the Foundation Representative, the Academic Coordinator and the DSL give a joint briefing instead.

tasks.title: Read your new principal's School State Report
tasks.description: A one-page picture of strengths and concerns from staff, parents and students after the Listen window. It is for information — not an approval step.
tasks.timing_text: End of Window 1, about 90 days after the principal starts (date shown assumes a July start)

source.quote: plus one paragraph of your own observation. Shared with your mentor and Foundation Rep.

tasks.title: Sign off your new principal's 3-Priority School Plan
tasks.description: The mentor reviews the plan first; you sign it off before the principal presents it at the term-opening staff meeting.
tasks.timing_text: End of Window 2 — before the term-opening staff meeting (date shown assumes a July start)

source.quote: Reviewed by your mentor; signed off by your Foundation Rep before you present it to staff.

tasks.title: Hold a mid-window check-in with your new principal
tasks.description: Check progress on Priority 1 during the Act window. The principal also shares a one-page Mid-Year Reflection with you and the mentor in this window.
tasks.timing_text: Middle of Window 3 (days 181–270; date shown assumes a July start)

source.quote: Priority 1 action sprint. Visible, weekly-documented work. A mid-window check-in with your Foundation Rep.

tasks.title: Receive your new principal's End-of-Year Report and Year-2 plan
tasks.description: Use them for Year-2 planning and continuity — goals, support and priorities — not as a performance judgement; the induction year is never scored. If the first year needs more time, that is handled through your review, not an automatic extension.
tasks.timing_text: End of Window 4 (the principal's first 12 months)

source.quote: Write your End-of-Year Principal Report (3 pages). Reviewed by your mentor; received by your Foundation Rep and the Executive Director.

tasks.title: Take part in the Foundations Mapping self-audit
tasks.description: With the principal and Academic Coordinator, work through an honest, no-scoring self-audit of all five domains with your Onboarding Supervisor. First adopt the Safeguarding & Child Protection Policy and name a Designated Safeguarding Lead.
tasks.applies_when: Your school is in its first year as an Eduversal partner

source.quote: Your leadership team owns the onboarding process. Your job is to engage honestly with the Foundations Mapping self-audit

tasks.title: Agree the focus of the school's Readiness Checkpoint
tasks.description: Before the Readiness Review Visit, the leadership team and the Onboarding Supervisor agree what to look at across the five domains. The outcome is Ready or Not Yet Ready — never a Development Rating.
tasks.applies_when: Your school is in its first year as an Eduversal partner

source.quote: Pre-conference: your leadership team and Onboarding Supervisor agree on the focus, covering all 5 domains.

notes_for_reviewer: Source title: the Career Growth framework export carries the internal title 'Eduversal Career Growth Framework' (Version 2.1); the Drive file name suggests 'Career Growth Framework 26-27'. Please confirm the exact live title for sources.cgf.

FR2-007: the School Appraisal Handbook says the Annual School Quality Report is 'shared with school leadership' and the appeal is made by 'a school's leadership'. It does not name the FR/GM; the FR/GM is counted as school leadership because 'Induction Module: School 26-27' defines the school leadership team as 'Foundation Representative, Principal, Academic Coordinator'. Confirm.

Phase 4 Impact Review (May–Jun 2027, online) gives no part to the FR/GM ('the school reviews', 'Led by the Visit I Supervisor with an Eduversal representative'), and it falls after the last teaching week. No FR/GM task was created. If the FR/GM should join it, the School Appraisal Handbook needs to say so.

EASE Growth: 'Reporting Formats Reference 26-27' proposes a one-page 'Results at a glance' for the FR/GM (four questions to ask the Principal), but marks it 'Proposed — pending Academic Board approval' and 'do not send them to schools'. No task was created. Once approved, add an FR/GM task: read the page when it is released with the School Baseline Summary and discuss the four questions with the principal.

Possible conflict with the no-single-school-score rule: 'Appraisal Suite: School Performance 26-27' says it 'belongs to the institutional line: the school's GM / Foundation Representative' and produces an 'Institutional operational signal on a 0–100 scale' with a 'TOTAL SCORE'. It says it is not the Development Rating, but it is still one number per school. It was not used as a task source.

Escalation inconsistency: 'Induction Module: Training Deck 26-27' says the Foundation Representative is the 'Escalation point if the mentor or HQ is the concern', while 'Induction Module: Principal 26-27' says 'concerns involving your Foundation Rep or Eduversal itself go to the Executive Director (Level 4)' and puts the FR at Level 2 after the mentor. The deck also uses 'HQ'. The tasks follow the Principal handbook.

Year-1 principal tasks (FR2-011 to FR2-014) follow the principal's own start date (windows of about 90 days). The placements assume a principal who starts in the first teaching week (13 July 2026): Window 1 ends about 10 October, Window 2 about 8 January (before the term-opening staff meeting on 4 January), Window 3 runs about 9 January–9 April. A principal who starts mid-year needs different weeks.
Principal Appraisal sign-off happens at 'year end'; the final conversation and the FR/GM co-signature may fall after the last teaching week (7 May 2027). FR2-008 is placed in the last teaching week.

Appointments: the Career Growth Framework says the Principal is 'appointed through Foundation governance under the FR/GM structure' but gives no step the FR/GM must take, so no separate principal-appointment task was created; FR2-004 covers Academic Coordinator / Vice Principal confirmations, which the framework gives to the FR/GM explicitly.

The Principal Appraisal summary the FR/GM receives includes the principal's 'composite score'. This is the principal's own appraisal result, not a school score; the task text says 'summary result' to avoid confusion with the school-level no-composite rule.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A monthly review of the leadership dashboard with the principal and leadership team, with the FR/GM as strategic adviser.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: Gives the FR/GM a regular, light touchpoint with the principal between appraisal events, which the live documents do not define.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Career Growth Framework 26-27 (FR/GM role) or Appraisal Suite: Master Overview 26-27

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A regular review of the school budget (RKAS) execution with the principal.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The Principals Checklist asks principals to track spending against the budget each term, but no live document says what the FR/GM does with it.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Quality Ecosystem: School Principals Checklist 26-27 or a new FR/GM role profile

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: FR/GM attendance at the Eduversal Leadership Camp / annual school leadership workshop.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The network calendar has Leadership Camp weeks (14–18 December 2026, 24–28 May 2027) but no live document says who attends.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.suggested_live_doc: Network calendar or Career Growth Framework 26-27

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: An annual review of the school's vision and mission, led by the principal with the FR/GM.
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The Principals Checklist asks principals to review vision and mission; the FR/GM, as the highest school-level governance authority, has no stated part.

ideas_not_in_live_docs.idea: A short weekly or fortnightly governance update from the principal to the FR/GM (reframed from the v1 yayasan digest).
ideas_not_in_live_docs.why_useful: The FR/GM is the principal's line manager, but the live documents give no regular reporting rhythm outside induction and appraisal.
